Triggers.value: Similar weather conditions to when the event happened

Maladaptive Strategies.value: keep mind occupied all the time

Threat.value: I listen for sounds that might mean someone is entering my home
My body reacts to danger before I have even had time to think
I jump or startle at ordinary sounds that would not bother most people

Memory.value: The memory is so extreme it is hard to believe it actually happened to me
When I think about the frightening event I can sometimes smell things that I smelt when the frightening event happened.
The memory feels like it belongs to someone else rather than to me

Negative Appraisals.value: The world is a dangerous place
I am no longer capable of doing the things that defined me
I can no longer trust my own body

vignette: Akua's eyes would often glaze over, lost in thought, as she worked on the factory floor. The hum of machinery and chatter of coworkers faded into the background when the air grew thick with heat, reminiscent of that sweltering day in the detention center. She couldn't shake the smell of sweat and urine, which transported her back to the cramped cell where she was held captive for weeks. The memories of torture still felt like a dream, too extreme to be real – but the scent brought it all flooding back. As she worked, Akua's senses were on high alert, listening for any unusual sounds that might signal someone approaching. She would startle at the slightest noise, her body reacting before her mind could catch up. The factory's echoing corridors made every footstep sound ominous, and she found herself constantly scanning her surroundings, searching for potential threats. Her coworkers began to notice her jumpiness, but Akua couldn't explain why; even she didn't fully understand. To cope with the anxiety that gripped her daily life, Akua developed a habit of applying heavy makeup before leaving home. It was as if a layer of foundation and mascara could shield her from the world's dangers, or at least make her feel more in control. She also kept herself occupied by mentally replaying conversations, rehashing arguments with her ex-husband, or planning elaborate meals – anything to distract herself from the thoughts that crept in when she was still. Akua's perception of the world had shifted irrevocably since her captivity. She now saw it as a treacherous place, where anyone could be a potential threat. This fear seeped into every aspect of her life, making her question her own capabilities and trust her body less with each passing day. The memories of torture only served to reinforce these negative appraisals – they felt like someone else's story, not hers. Avoiding clothes that resembled those she wore during captivity had become an unconscious habit for Akua. She wouldn't even notice it herself until a friend pointed out the sudden change in her wardrobe. Yet, when confronted with a familiar name or hearing a sound similar to the ones from that day, Akua would freeze – as if caught between past and present. As time passed, Akua found herself increasingly withdrawn. Her social life dwindled to almost nothing, and even interactions with coworkers became strained. She couldn't shake the feeling that she was living in a constant state of hypervigilance, ready for the next attack or threat at any moment. It was as if her body had become hardwired to respond before her mind could catch up. Akua knew this couldn't continue; the world might be a treacherous place, but she couldn't let fear consume her entirely. When a particularly severe panic attack left her shaken and unable to work for several days, Akua realized it was time to seek help – not just to learn how to manage her symptoms, but to reclaim some semblance of control over her life. What brought Akua to therapy was the desperate hope that she could learn to quiet the constant din of threat monitoring in her mind. She longed to be able to walk down a street without scanning every face for potential danger or hearing footsteps behind her. More than anything, she yearned to rediscover the woman she once was – capable and strong – before captivity shattered her world. As Akua sat in the therapist's office, surrounded by an unfamiliar yet calming environment, she knew this would be just the beginning of a long journey toward healing and reclaiming her life from the grip of PTSD.
